newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ fine wool prices improve at sales.
newsitem.headline: NZ fine wool prices improve at sales.

text.p: New Zealand fine wool prices improved, reflecting a rise in Australia, while crossbreds were unchanged and lambswool generally eased at sales in Napier and Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The provisional market indicator was up four cents to 443, with fine up 38 to 856, medium up eight to 534, strong down two to 388, and lamb down eight to 395.
On offer was 4,636 clean tonnes in 39,292 bales, chiefly comprising 35 percent crossbred fleece, 24 percent lambswool and 15 percent second shear. Passings amounted to 23 percent.

Compared with last week, merino fleece 17 micron and finer was 10 to 15 percent dearer and 18-23 micron up to 2.5 percent dearer. Halfbred fleece was up to 2.5 percent dearer. Crossbred 32-34 micron was unchanged, while 35 and stronger was par to two percent cheaper. Cotts were par to 2.5 percent cheaper.

First lambs in the North Island were up to 1.5 percent dearer for 28 micron, 2.5-5 percent cheaper for 29/30 micron and par to 1.5 percent cheaper for 31/32 micron. For the South Island they were generally unchanged.
Second lambs were 2.5-4 percent dearer, while bulky skirtings and second shear bellies and pieces were unchanged.
